title: ResNet
subtitle: {model.params} parameters · {model.input_shape} in, {node:n0250.out_shape[1]} classes out

stages.name: stem
stages.note: The one convolution outside a residual block. Its output is the tensor the first shortcut carries forward, which is why the arrow to the rejoin starts here.

stages.name: residual block
stages.note: One block opened so the reader can see what every later box contains. The shortcut is not drawn inside it: it is the edge that skips this stage entirely.

stages.name: shortcut rejoins
stages.note: The add is a real fork and rejoin in the trace: it consumes the stem's output and the main path's, which is what makes the bypass edge traced rather than asserted.

stages.name: the same block again
stages.note: Identical in structure to the two stages before it, shortcut included; collapsed because the anatomy has already been shown once. No repeat template is claimed anywhere in this figure: the widths differ in structure — the first block of each wider group carries a projection shortcut — so nothing tiles more than once, and a repetition that does not tile exactly must not be drawn as one.

stages.name: wider blocks, half the map
stages.note: Two blocks. The first strides and doubles the channels, so its shortcut cannot be the identity — a 1x1 convolution projects it, and that projection is the fork buried inside this box. The second block is an identity block like the two opened upstream.

stages.name: wider again, quarter the map
stages.note: The same pair again at the last width, and where most of the model's parameters are — a convolution's cost grows with the square of the channel count while the map it runs over shrinks only linearly in each axis.

stages.name: average over the map
stages.note: Global average pool and the flatten that follows it: the spatial axes go away here, which is why no glyph is drawn from this stage on — there is no map left to draw.

caption: The first block is opened — its convolutions beside the shortcut that skips them — so every collapsed box downstream can be read as the same pattern, with a projection standing in for the identity wherever the width changes. Each glyph is the tensor at that point: channels deep, the map as its face.
